tasks.title: control.ts link primitives + linked-death cascade + mailbox.ts bounded queue + sendInterAgentCommunication mailbox-full propagation
tasks.description: Foundation: D14 link primitives + D15 bounded mailbox + control wiring. (A) mailbox.ts — export `MAILBOX_DEFAULT_CAPACITY = 32` (top-level const); export `MailboxFullError extends Schema.TaggedErrorClass` with `{ capacity: Schema.Number }` field and `message` getter; extend `Interface` with `readonly send: (msg) => Effect<number, MailboxFullError>` (NOTE: signature changes — user sends can fail) AND `readonly sendSystem: (msg) => Effect<number>` (bypasses cap — no failure); extend `Mailbox.make` to take optional `capacity?: number` arg (defaults to MAILBOX_DEFAULT_CAPACITY); `send` checks `messages.length >= capacity` BEFORE atomic-modify and yields MailboxFullError if so; `sendSystem` skips the cap check (per WAVE.md gotcha 5 option (a): system-notification slot is conceptually separate even if implemented as same queue); update `Interface` JSDoc. (B) mailbox.test.ts — extend with: capacity defaults to 32; explicit capacity (e.g. 4) caps user sends; send returns MailboxFullError when capacity reached; sendSystem bypasses cap (succeeds after full); drain frees capacity for subsequent sends; concurrent sends past cap interleave between success+MailboxFullError correctly. Maintain 100% line coverage on mailbox.ts via single-file run. (C) control.ts — extend PerRootData with `links: Map<SessionID, Set<SessionID>>` (symmetric — entry stored on BOTH peers' Sets) AND `linkedDeathOf: Set<SessionID>` (marks sessions that the link cascade closed; the completion watcher consults to override the status label from 'shutdown' to 'linked_death' in the notification body). Initialize both fields in `ensureRootSlot`; clear in both the Session.Event.Deleted subscriber AND the disposal finalizer. (D) Add new Interface methods + Service.of bindings: `linkAgents(a: SessionID, b: SessionID, callerID: SessionID): Effect<void, AgentNotFoundError>` (per-root scoping — both a/b must resolve to same root via slotFor; idempotent — re-link is no-op; self-link rejected with AgentNotFoundError matching cross-root rejection shape via a sanity check or noop, prefer noop); `unlinkAgents(a, b, callerID): Effect<void>` (idempotent — unlink of non-linked pair is no-op, no error per WAVE.md gotcha 2); `agentLinks(id: SessionID, callerID: SessionID): Effect<readonly SessionID[]>` (returns the sorted SessionID[] of peers `id` is linked to; empty when no links — for tests + introspection). (E) Modify `sendInterAgentCommunication` signature: add optional `flags?: { system?: boolean }` parameter at end (default false → user); when `flags?.system === true`, route to mailbox.sendSystem (bypasses cap); when false/undefined, route to mailbox.send (returns MailboxFullError). Existing typed-error signature widens: `Effect<void, AgentNotFoundError | MailboxFullError>`. (F) Update existing internal callers in control.ts to opt into system path so completion notifications don't get blocked by user backpressure: respawn-cap branch at line ~1025 AND completion-watcher's main send at line ~1149 BOTH pass `{ system: true }`. spawnAgent's initial mailbox.send for the seed message (line ~897) calls `mailbox.sendSystem` directly (or sendInterAgentCommunication with system flag — sendSystem direct is shorter). (G) Completion-watcher cascade: after the standard notification is sent in the watcher (after the `sendInterAgentCommunication` call at line ~1149), but BEFORE the `if (isShutdown) return yield* Effect.interrupt` check, when the child reaches terminal NON-shutdown (isShutdown=false — i.e. completed or errored), iterate `slot.links.get(child.id) ?? new Set()` and for each peer `peerID`: if peer's status is non-final AND peer is not already in `linkedDeathOf`, add `peerID` to `linkedDeathOf` and call `closeAgent(peerID, child.id).pipe(Effect.catch(() => Effect.void))`. Cleanup: also clear the child.id from peer's `links.get(peerID)` sets and delete its own entry from `slot.links`. (H) Override the watcher's `label` for shutdown when linkedDeathOf is set: change `const label = isShutdown ? 'shutdown' : ...` to `const label = isShutdown ? (slot.linkedDeathOf.has(child.id) ? 'linked_death' : 'shutdown') : ...`. (I) Per-root scoping: linkAgents/unlinkAgents/agentLinks use `slotFor(data, callerID)`; verify both a and b resolve to the same slot (cross-root → AgentNotFoundError matching cross-root-send-rejection shape). (J) control.test.ts — add a `describe('AgentControl D14 link primitives')` block with >=8 it.live tests covering: link/unlink basic flow (link makes peers reciprocally tracked via agentLinks; unlink clears); link is symmetric (link(a,b) === link(b,a)); link is idempotent (re-link = no-op); unlink is idempotent (no error on unlinked pair); link across roots rejected with AgentNotFoundError; agentLinks for unknown id returns empty array; (cascade tests use registerRunLoop with Effect.die to crash one peer — assert the other transitions to shutdown WITHIN ~200ms via subscribeStatus). Also add a `describe('AgentControl D15 mailbox-full propagation')` block with >=4 it.live tests covering: sendInterAgentCommunication without flags returns MailboxFullError when target mailbox is at capacity (use a mailbox cap override path OR set capacity in test setup); sendInterAgentCommunication with { system: true } succeeds when at capacity (bypass); after drain, sends succeed again; the completion-watcher's notification path uses the system flag (verified via: fill child's mailbox to cap, close child, assert parent's mailbox still receives the completion notification). Maintain 100% line coverage on control.ts (function% may stay at the pre-existing Schema.TaggedErrorClass-quirk baseline per GOTCHA `schema-class-function-coverage`). (K) Gotchas to honor: Effect v4 (`Effect.fn`, `Effect.gen`, `Effect.forkIn` — no `Effect.fork`); flat exports + self-reexport at bottom (`export * as Mailbox from './mailbox'` — already present); per-root scoping non-negotiable (every new method takes callerID); no mocks of real surfaces; module-shape rules in packages/opencode/AGENTS.md.

tasks.title: agent-link tool — NEW directory packages/opencode/src/tool/agent-link/ with link_agents + unlink_agents tools + tests + registry+permission wiring
tasks.description: Wire the agent-link surface and the new tools into the runtime. (A) `agent-link/agent-link.ts` — single file with TWO exported Tool.define values (LinkAgentsTool + UnlinkAgentsTool), mirroring agent-wait/agent-wait.ts (AgentWaitTool + AgentWaitForReplyTool precedent). Constants: `LINK_ID = 'link_agents' as const`, `UNLINK_ID = 'unlink_agents' as const`, `PermissionKey = 'task' as const` (collapses onto MULTI_AGENT_TOOLS). Parameters Schema for link_agents (and identical for unlink_agents): Schema.Struct({ target_a: Schema.String (annotated: 'first agent. Relative path (worker_a) or canonical /root/...'), target_b: Schema.String (annotated: 'second agent. Same format as target_a.') }). Execute body for LinkAgentsTool: resolve currentPath via AgentToolContext.currentAgentPath; resolve both target_a + target_b via control.resolveAgentReference wrapped in Effect.result (target_not_found errorOutput shape on either failure); reject self-link (target_a resolves to same SessionID as target_b → errorOutput tag='self_link', output='cannot link an agent to itself'); ctx.ask permission with patterns: [`link:${target_a}|${target_b}`], always: ['*'], metadata: { target_a, target_b, target_a_session_id, target_b_session_id }; call control.linkAgents(idA, idB, ctx.sessionID) wrapped in Effect.result; on AgentNotFoundError return errorOutput tag='cross_root' (output: 'agents must belong to the same root'); on success return { title: `link_agents ${target_a} ↔ ${target_b}`, metadata: { target_a, target_b, linked: true }, output: 'Linked' }. UnlinkAgentsTool body is identical EXCEPT: no self-link rejection (unlink of self is no-op anyway); calls control.unlinkAgents; success output: 'Unlinked'; both error tags adapt the operation name. Both tools mirror the import + style + JSDoc shape of agent-pool/agent-pool.ts and agent-wait/agent-wait.ts. (B) `agent-link.txt` — Codex-quality tool description in the codemaxxxing voice with sections: brief one-paragraph intro explaining link is bidirectional-death (when either crashes, the runtime closes the other within ~100ms); 'When to use' (paired actors: generator/evaluator, prosecutor/defense, worker/verifier); 'When NOT to use' (loose coupling — don't link long-running peers that should survive individual failures); 'Linking semantics' (symmetric — link(a,b) === link(b,a); idempotent; survives across pool_strategy and on_failure — link is its own mechanism, fires before pool_strategy can react); 'Cross-root' (must be in same root; rejected with cross_root); 'Unlinking' (cheap, idempotent, no-op on unlinked pair); 'Cost' (one Map entry per pair per peer slot; cheap). Document both link_agents AND unlink_agents in this same .txt — both tools import DESCRIPTION from this file (mirrors how agent-wait imports two .txt files, but for simplicity here use ONE .txt and split via section headers, OR include both descriptions in one file and let each tool pick by section — choose whichever is cleaner. Recommendation: use ONE description file with ## link_agents AND ## unlink_agents sections, both tools import the file). 80-150 lines target. (C) `agent-link.test.ts` — testEffect layer mirroring agent-pool.test.ts; >=12 it.live (or it.instance via provideTmpdirInstance) tests: ID/PermissionKey assertions; Schema decode success/failure cases (missing target_a, missing target_b, both empty); link_agents happy path (link succeeds → metadata.linked === true); link_agents self-link rejected (tag='self_link'); link_agents cross-root rejected (tag='cross_root'); link_agents calls ctx.ask with the patterns array (record-based ctx); link_agents resolve failure for target_a → tag='target_not_found'; link_agents resolve failure for target_b → tag='target_not_found'; unlink_agents happy path (after a prior link, unlink succeeds); unlink_agents on unlinked pair is no-op (returns success, no error); unlink_agents cross-root rejected; unlink_agents resolve failure → tag='target_not_found'. Maintain 100% line coverage on agent-link.ts via single-file run. (D) Wire into runtime — `permission/index.ts` MULTI_AGENT_TOOLS at L336-345: insert 'link_agents' and 'unlink_agents' (preserve canonical order — add after 'spawn_pool'). `permission/disabled.test.ts` — update the 'MULTI_AGENT_TOOLS exports task + N v2 multi-agent IDs in canonical order' test to include link_agents + unlink_agents; extend the 'groups MULTI_AGENT_TOOLS under task key' test to verify both new tools are stripped on wildcard deny. `tool/registry.ts` — add `import { LinkAgentsTool, UnlinkAgentsTool } from './agent-link/agent-link'`; resolve via `const linkagents = yield* LinkAgentsTool` + `const unlinkagents = yield* UnlinkAgentsTool`; add `linkagents: Tool.init(linkagents)` and `unlinkagents: Tool.init(unlinkagents)` to the Effect.all object; add `tool.linkagents` and `tool.unlinkagents` to the builtin array adjacent to tool.agentpool; extend the legacy-bridge OR chain (currently includes AgentPoolTool.id) to also include `LinkAgentsTool.id` and `UnlinkAgentsTool.id` so the plugin hook routes through legacy 'task' ID. (E) Constraints: NO new describe* function needed (link doesn't render templated content). Maintain idiomatic code throughout — mirror existing patterns from agent-pool.ts (errorOutput helper, etc.). (F) Gotchas: tool descriptions are PROMPTS not labels — write in operational-manual voice per agent-pool.txt precedent; PermissionKey collapse onto 'task' is non-negotiable (gotcha `permission-key-collapse-needs-dual-write-evaluate-vs-disabled`); Effect v4 conventions throughout.

tasks.title: agent-send + agent-followup mailbox_full handling + tests
tasks.description: Make the existing user-facing tools surface mailbox-full as a structured tool error. (A) `agent-send.ts` — already wraps sendInterAgentCommunication in Effect.result + branches on AgentNotFoundError ('send_failed'). Extend the branch: when the failure tag is 'MailboxFullError', return a distinct shape: `{ title, metadata: { target, target_session_id, error: 'mailbox_full', retry_after_ms: <hint, e.g. 250> }, output: 'Mailbox full for ${target}; retry after ~${retry_after_ms}ms or use followup_task to wake recipient to drain' }`. Compute retry_after_ms from the MailboxFullError payload if it carries one (T1 may store capacity inside the error class but not retry_after_ms — hardcode 250ms here). Preserve the AgentNotFoundError branch as 'send_failed'. Both branches return rather than throw — model-recoverable. (B) `agent-followup.ts` — same shape adaptation. The current code uses Effect.orDie on sendInterAgentCommunication because the call site previously guaranteed AgentNotFoundError was unreachable. With MailboxFullError now possible, REPLACE the Effect.orDie with Effect.result; on AgentNotFoundError keep the prior (now-defensive) defect-like surface OR convert to a 'send_failed' error tag for consistency with agent-send; on MailboxFullError return the same mailbox_full shape with the followup_task wording adjusted: 'Mailbox full for ${target}; retry after ~${retry_after_ms}ms (followup_task does NOT bypass backpressure)'. Preserve the existing trigger_turn: true behavior — the mailbox_full check happens BEFORE the queue accepts, so trigger_turn is moot when full. (C) `agent-send.test.ts` — extend with: mailbox_full case returns the structured error tag + retry_after_ms; AgentNotFoundError case still returns 'send_failed' (regression-resistant); the success case still returns 'queued: true'. (D) `agent-followup.test.ts` — same shape: mailbox_full case returns the new tag; reject-root case unchanged; AgentNotFoundError case (now reachable via Effect.result, not Effect.orDie) returns 'send_failed' (regression-resistant). (E) Per-file 100% line coverage on agent-send.ts AND agent-followup.ts via single-file run. (F) The tests MUST trigger MailboxFullError end-to-end (not by mocking) — set up a real AgentControl with a child whose mailbox is at capacity (use a small capacity override exposed in test setup, OR fill via N sends until capacity is reached). Look at agent-pool.test.ts + agent-send.test.ts existing patterns for ctx setup and Effect.result handling. (G) Gotchas: no mocks of multi-agent surface; the existing 'send_failed' tag must not change shape (regression risk); Effect v4 conventions; do NOT add backwards-compat shims — change the orDie to result cleanly.

tasks.title: INV-D-21..23 integration invariants + multi-agent prose updates + prose enforcement test extensions
tasks.description: Lock in the contract via integration invariants and prose. (A) `multi-agent-invariants.test.ts` — append three new it.instance blocks INSIDE the existing `describe('INTEGRATION_INVARIANTS — multi-agent surfaces')` block, AFTER the INV-D-20 block (around L2385). Tests MUST run RED against pre-T1 code and GREEN against post-T1 code; if a test passes against the broken code, it's wrong — rewrite. (i) `INV-D-21-link-paired-death-on-either-crash`: registerRunLoop with a counter-based dispatch (worker A crashes via Effect.die OR uses sendInterAgentCommunication then exits; worker B uses Effect.never to stay idle). Spawn root; spawn /root/peer_a and /root/peer_b; control.linkAgents(idA, idB, root.id); subscribe to peer_b's status; crash peer_a (have its runLoop yield* Effect.die / let its fiber fail); within ~500ms (use SubscriptionRef.changes wait or polling), peer_b's status transitions to 'shutdown'. Then assert: parent's mailbox contains a completion notification for peer_b whose body header reads 'reached status: linked_death' (the label override). Symmetric variant: in a separate test, crash peer_b first → peer_a closed with linked_death. Third sub-test: after unlinkAgents(idA, idB), crashing peer_a does NOT close peer_b. (ii) `INV-D-22-bounded-mailbox-rejects-on-overflow`: spawn root; spawn one child; override the child's mailbox capacity to 4 (either via a test-only mailbox.make(4) helper exposed by T1, OR by spawning agents with a per-spawn cap input if T1 adds one, OR by sending until the system default 32 is exceeded — choose whichever T1 chose). Call control.sendInterAgentCommunication(childID, comm, root.id) 5 times (the 5th send should fail); first 4 succeed; the 5th call returns Effect.result success with MailboxFullError; mailbox.peek confirms 4 items in order; sixth call still fails; after drainMailbox, subsequent sends succeed. (iii) `INV-D-23-bounded-mailbox-does-not-block-completion-notification`: same mailbox-at-capacity setup as INV-D-22 but for the CHILD's mailbox; arrange the child to terminate (registerRunLoop that emits text + close_agent or fails); assert the PARENT's mailbox receives the completion notification (system path) regardless of the child's mailbox state. If the child's mailbox is the one that's full, the completion-watcher writes to PARENT's mailbox — verify the parent gets the notification AND that the system-bypass on PARENT'S mailbox (not child's) is what mattered — re-read T1's implementation to align the test scenario with the actual code path. The KEY assertion: the parent's mailbox notification arrives, with the standard 'Agent <child path> reached status:' body. (B) `multi-agent-root.txt` — extend the `## Limits` section with a NEW bullet point about bounded mailboxes + backpressure: '**bounded mailboxes — sends can fail.** Each agent's mailbox has a finite capacity (default 32 user messages). When you `send_message` or `followup_task` to a peer whose mailbox is at capacity, the call returns `{ error: "mailbox_full", retry_after_ms: <hint> }` instead of queueing. Retry after a backoff, or use `followup_task` to wake the recipient so they drain. Completion notifications from terminating subagents bypass this cap — your subagent crashing always notifies you regardless of mailbox state.' Place this bullet AFTER the existing 'idle ≠ alive' bullet. (C) `multi-agent-subagent.txt` — extend the cross-agent messaging section with a brief mention: AFTER the `wait_for_reply` bullet, add a paragraph: 'Mailbox backpressure: `send_message` / `followup_task` can fail with `mailbox_full` when the recipient is over capacity. Treat it like any tool-recoverable error — retry with a small backoff (~250ms) or switch to `followup_task` to ensure the recipient wakes and drains. The recipient is alive; their queue is just full.' Place between the 'cross-agent messaging' bullet list and the 'You cannot followup_task the root agent' line. (D) `prose/subagent-prompts.test.ts` — extend with: new tests asserting multi-agent-root.txt contains 'bounded mailboxes' (case-insensitive) AND 'mailbox_full' AND 'completion notifications from terminating subagents bypass this cap' (or similar phrase from above); multi-agent-subagent.txt contains 'mailbox_full' AND 'retry with a small backoff'. Also add a test asserting agent-link.txt exists (file presence) and contains substrings 'bidirectional' OR 'paired death' OR 'linked'. (E) The invariant tests target the surface T1+T2+T3 ship; if they don't run RED against the un-shipped surface, the test is wrong. Use it.instance + provideTmpdirInstance like the existing INV-D-* tests (see L2171+ for the spawn_pool invariant patterns). (F) Gotchas: integration-first discipline (every code surface MUST have at least one it.instance test against an invariant — INV-D-21/22/23 satisfy this); 100% per-file line coverage on the modified prose-test file via single-file run; do NOT change tests' shape to match buggy code — fix the code if a test fails legitimately.

anti_patterns_to_flag: any new method that walks every root (per-root scoping invariant)
any mock of AgentControl / Mailbox / Session in tests for the surfaces under test
any backwards-compat shim that defers a clean change
any prose phrase suggesting text is the deliverable (D1 invariant must not regress)
any prose duplicating between root and subagent files (PROMPT_SURFACES ownership map)
